profile.summary: An endemic shrub with widely spreading branches and small rounded leaves. Young plants can have leaves divided into three leaflets.
profile.lookFor: Small thick leaves with finely roughened margins and a joint where each blade meets its flattened stalk. Cream star-shaped flowers are followed by dry fruit divided into several parts.

profile.summary: An endemic broom with rigid branching stems and few visible leaves. Its yellowish branchlets are grooved, and small cream to pale pink pea flowers form clusters along them.
profile.lookFor: Stout grooved branchlets and tightly grouped pea flowers, often with purple markings. Small dry pods follow flowering; subspecies identification needs closer botanical examination.

profile.nameNote: Horopito is shared with other Pseudowintera species; NZPCN calls this one red or mountain horopito.
profile.summary: An endemic shrub of forest edges and scrub through the North, South and Stewart islands. Its leaf colouring becomes especially conspicuous in exposed places.
profile.lookFor: Matte green to yellow-green oval leaves often blotched red, with pale whitish undersides. Dark branchlets bear small yellow-green flowers and dark red or black berries.

profile.nameNote: Flora of New Zealand records Tōtara and Amoka. Tōtara also occurs in names of other Podocarpus species; no variety is assigned to this species-level record.
profile.summary: An endemic conifer that can become a large forest tree. Mature trees have thick stringy bark and a broad spreading crown.
profile.lookFor: Stiff narrow pointed leaves on woody branchlets. Older trunks show deep furrows and long fibrous bark strips.
